deep_dive.title: An Equivariant Filter for Spacecraft Nonlinear Relative Navigation with Range and Bearing Measurements
deep_dive.abstract: Relative navigation is a fundamental task in space proximity operations and autonomous rendezvous. The nonlinear relative orbital dynamics are equivariant and admit a semidirect product Lie group symmetry. This property is used to design an Equivariant Filter (EqF). The filter estimates the relative position and velocity between a chaser spacecraft and a target by lifting the filter dynamics to the group, while respecting the underlying geometry of the problem. Simulations demonstrate the filter's performance and effectiveness.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Relative navigation is central to autonomous rendezvous and proximity operations. Exploiting the semidirect product Lie group symmetry of relative orbital dynamics, the authors design an Equivariant Filter estimating relative position and velocity from range and bearing measurements.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 相对导航是空间近距操作与自主交会对接的核心任务，但相对轨道动力学的强非线性给滤波估计带来困难。本文利用相对轨道动力学具有半直积李群对称性这一性质，将滤波动力学提升到群上，设计出尊重问题几何结构的等变滤波器，用以从距离和方位测量中估计追踪器与目标航天器之间的相对位置和速度。仿真实验验证了该滤波器的性能与有效性。该工作为月面及地月空间自主接近导航提供了具有几何一致性的估计方法。

quick_skim.title: TEMPUS: Relativistic coordinate time scales for any solar-system body from arbitrary ephemerides
quick_skim.abstract: Precise time-scale transformations between solar-system bodies are an essential requirement for deep-space science and solar system navigation. The post-Newtonian relativistic expression relating a body-centered coordinate time TCX to the Barycentric Coordinate Time TCB depends on the gravitational environment and velocity of the target body, and must be evaluated consistently with the chosen planetary ephemerides. So far only INPOP has provided such a solution as part of its ephemerides releases, albeit only for Earth with TCG-TCB. We present TEMPUS, a tool that numerically integrates the IAU 2000 time-transformation for any solar-system body using positions and velocities from an arbitrary ephemerides. We provide a validated, ephemerides-agnostic implementation of TCX-TCB and assess its accuracy against published independent solutions. The rate $d\,\mathrm{TCX}/d\,\mathrm{TCB}$ is integrated with an Adams-Moulton order-12 predictor-corrector. The gravitational potential sum tested here includes the Sun, eight planets, Pluto, up to 343 main-belt asteroids, and 30 trans-Neptunian objects. Outputs can be stored in readable format tables of sampled values or as Chebyshev coefficient files. Comparisons are performed against the TU Dresden Klioner time solutions, the TCG-TCB solution provided with INPOP19a and INPOP21a, and the LTE440 lunar solution. For the planetary bodies TEMPUS agrees with Klioner at the $10^{-21} s\,s^{-1}$ level over 200 yr. Against the INPOP19a released TCG-TCB we also agree to the same level. The main-belt asteroids as well as the trans-Neptunian objects shift the planetary time scales at the $10^{-18} s\,s^{-1}$ level, and the choice of planetary and lunar ephemerides contributes differences on the $10^{-18} s\,s^{-1}$ level as well. TEMPUS provides a validated, ephemeris-agnostic post-Newtonian time-transformation for any solar-system body.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: TEMPUS numerically integrates the IAU 2000 time transformation using positions and velocities from arbitrary ephemerides to produce body-centered coordinate times for any solar-system body, extending relativistic timing needed for deep-space navigation and time transfer.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 深空科学与太阳系导航需要天体间精确的时间尺度转换，而此前仅有INPOP对地球给出TCG-TCB解。本文提出TEMPUS，利用任意星历提供的位置与速度对IAU 2000时间转换公式进行数值积分，可为任意太阳系天体生成TCX-TCB坐标时间。结果验证了该工具的正确性，将授时能力扩展到全部太阳系天体。该工作对地月空间及深空导航的多源定位授时具有支撑意义。
